name: GenLimit.Angluin.TheoremTwoStatement
reconstruction: This declaration defines a proposition; it does not prove that proposition. Its value says: there exists an EffectiveIndexedFamily F of nonempty subsets of Nat, with one total jointly computable exact Boolean membership function, such that (i) for each index i there exists a finite T_i⊆F.language i for which every family member F.language j containing T_i and contained in F.language i also contains all of F.language i; and (ii) no total computable function M : List Nat → Nat identifies the whole indexed family on all exact positive presentations. Identification here means: for every target index z and stream s with range(s)=F.language z, some index k denoting that same language is returned on every sufficiently long prefix of that particular stream. The single identifier M must precede and handle all z,s. The definition supplies neither an instance of F nor a proof that such an instance exists.

assumptions.outer_hypotheses: None: the target is a closed definition of type Prop, with no parameters or typeclass binders.
existential_family_fields: ∀ i x, membership i x=true ↔ x∈language i
assumptions.first_conjunct: ∀ i, ∃ T_i : Finset Nat, (T_i:Set Nat)⊆F.language i ∧ ∀ j, (T_i:Set Nat)⊆F.language j → F.language j⊆F.language i → F.language i⊆F.language j.
assumptions.second_conjunct: ¬∃ M : List Nat → Nat, Computable M ∧ ∀ z (s : Nat → Nat), Set.range s=F.language z → ∃ k, F.language k=F.language z ∧ ∃ N, ∀ t, N≤t → M(List.map s (List.range t))=k.
assumptions.dependency_order: F is chosen before both conjuncts. T_i may depend on F and i, and is fixed before j. The excluded M would be chosen before every z and whole stream s. Within each identification obligation k may depend on z,s, and N may additionally depend on k. No computable tell-tale selector or effective convergence threshold is assumed.

algorithm_and_access_boundary: No algorithm, emitter, oracle interface, update rule, concrete family witness, or construction is named by this proposition. F packages ordinary jointly computable membership. The excluded learner is a total ordinary computable history-to-index function, uniform in all targets and exact positive streams for one F; it is not a procedure with arbitrary additional oracle access. Tell-tales are only semantic finite-set existences. Histories are ordered finite lists retaining repetitions. Outputs are single Nat hypothesis names, with eventual exact index stability and denotation equality; there is no support-valued loss, distribution, randomization, novelty, bound or rate.
